html:
The Makurap are an Indigenous people of Rondônia in western Brazil, near the Guaporé River on the border with Bolivia. Their language belongs to the Tupari branch of the Tupian family, distant kin of the language of the Tupi of the coast.

In the early 1900s rubber tappers of the rubber boom moved into the Guaporé valley and took many Makurap to work on their estates, where epidemics killed many. Today they live mainly on the Rio Branco and Guaporé reserves with other peoples, such as the nearby Aikanã. Portuguese is now the main language of the young, but elders still use Makurap at festivals where chicha, a fermented drink, is shared.
